Homeownership is the cornerstone of the American Dream. 🇺🇸🏡

Too many young families and hardworking Americans are doing everything right and still can’t save enough for a down payment. That’s why I introduced the NEST Act, to help a new generation of homebuyers save responsibly, keep more of what they EARN, and build wealth they can pass down.

Here's what the NEST Act does: 

✅ Establishes tax-advantaged First-Time Homebuyer Savings Accounts under the Internal Revenue Code.

✅ Allows above-the-line tax-deductible contributions to help families save faster.

✅ Provides tax-free growth and tax-free withdrawals when used for qualified home purchase expenses.

✅ Permits funds to be used for down payments, closing costs, and related financing expenses for a primary residence.

✅ Limits eligibility to individuals who have not owned a principal residence within the prior three years.

✅ Caps lifetime contributions at 20 percent of the state median home price to reflect local housing markets.

✅ Allows employers to contribute to an employee’s account on a tax-free basis.

✅ Imposes taxes and penalties on non-qualified withdrawals to protect program integrity.

Your paycheck. Your future. Your first home. 

Let’s get this bill passed and make the American Dream a reality. 🇺🇲💪

When the cameras leave after a hurricane, the recovery is just getting started. Cedar Key knows that better than anyone.

This week, I was out on the water with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the City of Cedar Key, UF’s Nature Coast Biological Station, and the Cedar Key Aquaculture Association to see where things stand.

Idalia and Helene hit this community hard. On Seahorse Key, storm damage and erosion threaten the historic lighthouse and the cemetery where U.S. servicemembers and lighthouse keepers are laid to rest. That history deserves protecting.

We also toured the clam beds and oyster reef restoration that keep Levy County’s working waterfront going. Shellfish producers face challenges every storm season that federal disaster programs don’t always account for. That’s why I’ve cosponsored the Fair Access to Agriculture Disaster Programs Act and the Supporting Equity for Aquaculture and Seafood Act.

Recovery here will take years, and Cedar Key deserves a partner for the long haul. Thank you to everyone who hosted us and to the folks around town who stopped to say hello! 💙

I introduced H.Res. 500 to require criminal background checks for all House staff. Staffers in the People’s House handle sensitive information and work in positions of public trust. We need to know whether their history raises safety or security concerns BEFORE giving them that access.

This isn’t controversial. It’s common sense. 

The People’s House should be setting the standard. It’s time we met it.

Stronger infrastructure. Better storm preparedness. Less burden on local taxpayers. 🇺🇸

I secured $39.3 million in water and wastewater infrastructure authorization for Columbia and Suwannee counties in the House-passed Water Resources Development Act.

In Suwannee County, these improvements would help support a new regional emergency shelter for seniors, special-needs evacuees, and families fleeing coastal hurricanes. By building infrastructure that can handle a surge in population during emergencies, we're helping our communities prepare for the next storm without sticking local taxpayers with the bill.

https://t.co/oI9FStLxQH

The fact that Congress isn't doing this already is INSANE. 

Background checks should be mandatory for House staff. 

Pass H.Res. 500. Hold Congress to the same standards as everyone else. It's common sense. https://t.co/Qjn513zyBg

Happy 251st birthday to the U.S. Navy! ⚓🇺🇸

Since 1775, America’s sailors have answered the call to defend our freedom, keep our sea lanes open, and keep our adversaries in check.

Florida is proud to be home to so many who serve. Thousands of active duty sailors and even more veterans who chose to stay and raise their families here. We see you, and we’re grateful for you.

To everyone who has worn the uniform, and to the families who held it down at home: thank you for your service and your sacrifice. I’ll always have your back in Congress.💪🇺🇸

⚠️ Isaias has weakened, and all hurricane and tropical storm warnings have ended. Stay cautious, because hazards remain.

Rain is still falling across our district, and the Santa Fe and Suwannee rivers are still rising. Watch for standing water and downed power lines. If you evacuated, only return home when officials say it's safe. Never drive through flooded roads, and only run generators outdoors, at least 20 feet from your home.

📞 If you need help with FEMA or any federal agency, our office is here. Call 352-505-0838 or visit https://t.co/SXZXvpsw4u.

Check on your neighbors and stay safe!

I’m not in Congress to protect the status quo. I’m here to disrupt it.

100,000+ pages of regulations and endless red tape are making it harder to build, hire, produce, and grow, without making America safer or better.

It’s time to cut the red tape, tear down the barriers, and unleash the full power of the American economy.🇺🇸

🚨 Hurricane Isaias is now a Category 3. Here's what you need to know for our district.

🌊 Coast: A Storm Surge Warning covers the Dixie County coast, and Levy County is under a Storm Surge Watch. If officials tell you to evacuate, go.

🌧️ Inland: The ground is soaked and rivers are running high, so flooding can happen fast. Never drive through flooded roads.

Our office is standing by to help. Reach out at https://t.co/SXZXvpt3U2, and find the latest updates at https://t.co/k3hOoCk08b

🚨 HURRICANE ISAIAS UPDATE: A Storm Surge Warning is in effect for the entire Dixie County coast, including Horseshoe Beach and Suwannee, with up to 3 to 5 feet of surge possible. Levy County remains under a Storm Surge Watch. If officials tell you to evacuate, go.

Baker, Columbia, Dixie, Gilchrist, Hamilton, Lafayette, Levy and Suwannee counties are under a State of Emergency, and a Flood Watch is in effect for Marion County through late tonight. Across our district, the ground is already soaked and rivers are running high, so flooding can happen fast. Now is the time to prepare.

⚠️ Stay on top of local alerts and follow emergency officials' guidance.

🏠 Secure outdoor items and stock up on essentials.

🌊 Never drive through flooded roads.

🔌 Charge your devices and prepare for possible power outages.

📍 Stay informed:
• Hurricane updates: https://t.co/kKvqbDWF7g
• Florida emergency resources: https://t.co/rnBQDkIeVT
• Road conditions: https://t.co/tQ2O42FlOJ (https://t.co/m26Wp0LVZW)
• Local forecasts: https://t.co/cfipdr7fs8

My team and I are keeping a close eye on the storm and will share updates as they come in. Look out for your neighbors, be prepared, and stay safe!

🚨 Hurricane #Isaias: Storm Surge Warning for Dixie County

The National Hurricane Center has issued a Storm Surge Warning for the entire Dixie County coast, including Horseshoe Beach and Suwannee. Water could reach 3 to 5 feet above ground if peak surge hits at high tide.

This is life-threatening. If officials tell you to evacuate, go.

Levy County remains under a Storm Surge Watch, with 2 to 4 feet possible from the Suwannee River to Yankeetown. Cedar Key and Yankeetown, be ready to move.

Inland, our ground is already saturated. Parts of the Big Bend could see up to 15 inches of rain, and river flooding is expected. The tornado threat reaches North Florida on Saturday. Never drive through standing water.

Finish your preparations today:

✅ Charge phones and power banks
✅ Refill prescriptions
✅ Fill your gas tank
✅ Put important documents in a waterproof bag
✅ Secure anything outside that can blow away
✅ Decide where you'd go if you need to leave

Find your county emergency management office and the latest updates at https://t.co/k3hOoCjsiD.

⛈️ Isaias update for North Central Florida:

A Storm Surge Watch covers our coast in Dixie and Levy counties. The National Hurricane Center says water could reach 2 to 4 feet above ground from the Steinhatchee River to Yankeetown if peak surge hits at high tide.

If officials tell you to evacuate, go.

Isaias is expected to become a hurricane tomorrow morning and make landfall late Friday or early Saturday. Tornadoes are possible Friday evening into Saturday.

Inland, our lakes and rivers are already high. Standing water and flash flooding are the biggest threat for most of our district.

Find your county emergency management office and the latest updates at https://t.co/k3hOoCk08b.

You need a background check to work almost anywhere in America.

But not Congress. That’s insane.

I introduced H.Res. 500 to change it. If you work in the People’s House, a background check should be the bare minimum.

Call your representative. Tell them: cosponsor H.Res. 500. No more double standards.

Three years ago today, the world witnessed pure evil.

Hamas terrorists slaughtered roughly 1,200 innocent people—families in their homes, young people at a music festival, Americans, mothers, fathers, and children. Hundreds more were ripped from their families and taken hostage.

October 7th was terrorism. It was barbarism. And we will never forget.

Today, we remember the innocent lives stolen and pray for the families who carry that loss every day.

Our farmers feed America, and Washington needs to get out of their way. 

Florida's producers are facing rising costs and real uncertainty, and they deserve policies that help them compete, not red tape that holds them back. 

Get government out of the way and let our farmers do what they do best. 

I'll keep fighting for the farmers and families of North Central Florida. 🇺🇸

Gator Nation is coming to Capitol Hill! 🐊🇺🇸

The University of Florida is establishing the Ballard House steps from the U.S. Capitol, a permanent home for students, faculty, researchers, and alumni to learn, connect, and engage in our nation's capital.

Can't wait to see @UF grow its footprint in DC. GO GATORS! 🐊

Ready to serve? Applications for my Spring Internship Program are officially open! 🇺🇸

If you’re interested in public service and want a firsthand look at how Congress works, this is your chance to get hands-on experience in my Washington, D.C., Gainesville, or Ocala offices.

Interns work alongside Team Kat in communications, constituent services, legislative work, and the day-to-day operations of a congressional office.

To apply, submit:
✅ Resume
✅ Cover letter
✅ Two letters of recommendation
✅ Social media handles  

📩 Email your application to FL03.Internships@mail.house.gov by November 27 and specify which office you’re applying to.

Come see what public service looks like firsthand with Team Kat! 🇺🇸

This is HUGE news for the Gator Nation! 🐊

Team Kat helped secure $22.3 million for Alzheimer’s research, helping UF College of Medicine hit its biggest year ever for R&D funding, nearly $200 million!

I've spent years working alongside caregivers and families facing Alzheimer's and dementia, and I've seen firsthand what this disease takes from them. Better treatments can't come soon enough, and they start with research.

That's why this investment matters. Proud to partner with UF and the researchers leading the way right here in FL-03. 💪🇺🇸

Volunteers of America called us with a problem: homeless veterans in Ocala and Gainesville were at risk of losing their housing. I went straight to VA Secretary Collins, and our team stayed on it until a new contract kept a roof over their heads. 🇺🇸

Read the full article below ⬇️ 
https://t.co/8JGKSfaM8Y

Last month, Team Kat closed 290 cases and returned more than $431,000 to families across FL-03. Since I took office, we’ve helped bring $125.4 million back home.

Behind every dollar and every case is a real person who needed help. A veteran waiting on benefits. A senior fighting for Social Security. A family stuck in federal red tape.

That’s what constituent services are for. If you’re having trouble with a federal agency, call my office. We’ll go to work for you. 🇺🇸

It's time to stop talking about the next political fight and start building toward generational change.
Yes! And while we’re at it, how about the Senate pass the 600+ bills the House sent them? https://t.co/ooQLypdOEB

We owe veterans, active duty servicemembers, and their families a debt we will never be able to fully repay. 

For too long, we’ve walked back our promises to these brave men and women even after they’ve kept theirs. If you lost your husband or wife in service to our country, you shouldn’t have to choose between finding love again and keeping the benefits your family earned, and if you’re wounded in combat and medically retired, Washington shouldn’t dock your pay.🇺🇸

First responders run toward danger in our darkest moments. As the wife of a fire fighter and SWAT medic, I’ve seen the reality of that sacrifice up close. The weight they carry doesn't disappear when their shifts end.

That's why I introduced the Answering the Call Act to ensure the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is better equipped to support the men and women on the front lines. 

My bill strengthens mental health support for our first responders by requiring targeted outreach, expanding training and public awareness, and building stronger partnerships with organizations that understand the unique challenges they face. It also includes strong privacy safeguards to help ensure sensitive information is handled responsibly.

Our first responders put everything on the line to protect our communities. They deserve mental health resources that understand their experiences, respect their privacy, and provide the support they need when they need it most.

They've always had our backs. I'll always have theirs. 🇺🇸
